newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says may bring back students in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says may bring back students in Australia.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Monday the country might consider bringing back its students in Australia if reported threats against them were found to be serious.
"We want to get information on whether (the situation) is really dangerous. (If so) we will take action, whether by bringing them home or offering them protection," he told reporters.
Mahathir said he might even ask the Australian government to protect the students.
He said he had not received an official complaint from the Malaysian mission in Australia on the matter but had read press reports.

The national Bernama news agency reported on Sunday that a Malaysian student leader in Australia wanted the Malaysian and Australian governments to protect foreign students from racial abuse and threats.

She was quoted by Bernama as saying that several Malaysian students had had "nasty experiences" such as verbal abuse, since Australia was engulfed in a race row sparked by independent politician Pauline Hanson.
Hanson, in her maiden parliamentary speech in September, said Australia was being swamped by Asians and called for an immediate moratorium on immigration.
Asians make up about five percent of Australia's 18 million population.
More than 11,000 Malaysians are studying in Australia.
